# CAAM: China's new energy vehicle sales grew 37.9% to 9.495 million units in 2023, with a 31.6% market share

2024-01-11 15:07:51 Source: China Securities Network Author: Yu Liyan

Shanghai Securities News / China Securities Network (reporter Yu Liyan) - On 11 January, data released by the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers (CAAM) showed that in December 2023 China's new energy vehicle production and sales reached 1.172 million and 1.191 million units respectively, up 47.5% and 46.4% year over year, with a market share of 37.7%. For 2023 as a whole, China's new energy vehicle production and sales reached 9.587 million and 9.495 million units respectively, up 35.8% and 37.9% year over year, with a market share of 31.6%, 5.9 percentage points higher than the same period in 2022.

## New energy vehicle output exceeded 7 million units in 2022

Published: 2023/01/31

Source: China Association of Automobile Manufacturers

[ Print ]

According to China Association of Automobile Manufacturers statistics, new energy vehicle production and sales in 2022 reached 7.058 million and 6.887 million units respectively, up 96.9% and 93.4% year over year. Of these, new energy passenger vehicle production and sales reached 6.716 million and 6.549 million units, up 97.77% and 94.26% year over year; new energy commercial vehicle production and sales reached 342,000 and 338,000 units, up 81.84% and 78.89% year over year.

　　In December 2022, new energy vehicle production and sales reached 795,000 and 814,000 units, both up 51.8% year over year, of which new energy passenger vehicle production and sales reached 750,000 and 757,000 units, and new energy commercial vehicle production and sales reached 45,000 and 57,000 units.

## New energy vehicle production and sales, January-February 2021

Published: 2021/03/12

Source: Industry Department

[ Print ]

According to China Association of Automobile Manufacturers statistics, from January to February 2021 new energy vehicle production and sales reached 317,000 and 289,000 units respectively, up 3.9-fold and 3.2-fold year over year. Of these, battery electric vehicle production and sales reached 273,000 and 243,000 units, up 4.6-fold and 3.6-fold year over year; plug-in hybrid vehicle production and sales reached 44,000 and 46,000 units, up 1.7-fold and 1.8-fold year over year.

In February 2021 new energy vehicle production and sales reached 124,000 and 110,000 units, setting a new monthly sales record for the eighth consecutive month. Of these, battery electric vehicle production and sales reached 107,000 and 92,000 units; plug-in hybrid vehicle production and sales reached 16,000 and 17,000 units.

　　In January, vehicle exports were 301,000 units, up 30.1% year over year, of which passenger vehicle exports were 250,000 units, up 35.6% year over year, and commercial vehicle exports were 50,000 units, up 8.1% year over year. New energy vehicle exports were 83,000 units, up 48.2% year over year.

# China's 2022 vehicle sales reached 26.864 million units; new energy vehicle sales grew 93.4% year over year

2023-01-16 00:17:10

Source: Liaowang

On 12 January the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers released 2022 vehicle production and sales data. CAAM said that in 2022 vehicle production and sales grew steadily, the main economic indicators continued to improve, and the industry showed strong resilience, playing an important part in stabilising industrial economic growth.

　　Overall, 2022 vehicle production and sales reached 27.021 million and 26.864 million units respectively, up 3.4% and 2.1% year over year; compared with the previous year, output growth was flat while sales growth fell by 1.7 percentage points.

　　On new energy, 2022 saw continued explosive growth, with production and sales reaching 7.058 million and 6.887 million units respectively, up 96.9% and 93.4% year over year, and market share rising to 25.6% as the sector moves gradually into a phase of full market-driven expansion and a new stage of development and growth.

　　On domestic brands, Chinese-brand passenger vehicle sales in 2022 were 11.766 million units, up 22.8% year over year, with market share reaching 49.9%, up 5.4 percentage points.

## Brief analysis of new energy vehicle production and sales, July 2023

Published: 2023-08-18
Source: Industry Information Department, CAAM

　　According to China Association of Automobile Manufacturers statistical analysis, new energy vehicles continued their good momentum in July 2023.  
  
　　In July 2023, new energy vehicle production and sales reached 805,000 and 780,000 units respectively, with output up 2.8% month over month and sales down 3.2% month over month, and both up 30.6% and 31.6% year over year.  
  
　　From January to July 2023, new energy vehicle production and sales reached 4.591 million and 4.526 million units respectively, up 40% and 41.7% year over year.  
  
　　In July 2023, among the main new energy vehicle categories, compared with the previous month plug-in hybrid vehicle production and sales both grew slightly, battery electric vehicle output rose marginally while sales fell slightly, and fuel cell vehicle production and sales declined markedly; compared with the same period a year earlier, battery electric and plug-in hybrid vehicle production and sales grew to varying degrees, while fuel cell vehicle output fell and sales grew.  
  
　　From January to July 2023, among the main new energy vehicle categories, all three classes grew rapidly compared with the same period a year earlier.  
  
　　In July 2023, new energy vehicle domestic sales were 679,000 units, down 6.9% month over month and up 26% year over year.  
  
　　From January to July 2023, new energy vehicle domestic sales were 3.89 million units, up 32.5% year over year.  
  
　　In July 2023, new energy vehicle exports were 101,000 units, up 29.5% month over month and up 87% year over year.  
  
　　From January to July 2023, new energy vehicle exports were 636,000 units, up 1.5-fold year over year.

# CAAM: new energy vehicle market penetration reached 19.1% in December 2021

China News Finance, 19 January - On the 19th the "CAAM Data" WeChat official account published "Brief analysis of new energy vehicle production and sales, December 2021", showing that new energy vehicle market penetration reached 19.1% in December 2021.

　　According to China Association of Automobile Manufacturers statistical analysis, new energy vehicles were the automotive industry's biggest bright spot in 2021, leading the world in sales for the seventh consecutive year. Their market development has moved from a policy-driven to a market-pulled new stage of development, showing a healthy pattern of improvement in both market scale and quality of development, and laying a solid foundation for high-quality development of the automotive industry during the 14th Five-Year Plan.

　　The data shows that new energy vehicle market penetration reached 19.1% in December 2021, again higher than the previous month, with new energy passenger vehicle market penetration reaching 20.6%.

　　On production and sales volumes, in December 2021 new energy vehicle production and sales reached 518,000 and 531,000 units respectively, another record high, up 1.2-fold and 1.1-fold year over year.

　　For 2021 as a whole, new energy vehicle production and sales reached 3.545 million and 3.521 million units respectively, both up 1.6-fold year over year, with a market share of 13.4%, 8 percentage points higher than the previous year.

　　By segment, in December 2021 battery electric vehicles also set a new monthly production and sales record. Battery electric vehicle production and sales both grew 1.1-fold year over year; plug-in hybrid vehicle production and sales grew 1.6-fold and 1.2-fold year over year; fuel cell vehicle production and sales grew 1.4-fold and 1.1-fold year over year.

　　For 2021 as a whole, compared with the same period a year earlier, both battery electric and plug-in hybrid vehicle production and sales showed rapid growth momentum. (End)

# China's new energy vehicle sales grew 157.8% year over year in 2021

2022-07-20 09:18:56  Source: CCTV News client

Original headline: "Automotive Industry Blue Book" released today - China's new energy vehicle sales grew 157.8% year over year in 2021

　　Today (19 July), Social Sciences Academic Press, the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers and others jointly released the "Automotive Industry Blue Book: Report on the Development of China's Commercial Vehicle Industry (2022)".

　　The blue book notes that in 2021 the domestic new energy vehicle market developed rapidly, with full-year sales exceeding 3.5 million units, up 157.8% year over year, of which new energy commercial vehicle sales were 168,000 units, up 49.4% year over year, a penetration rate of 3.5%.

　　Under the country's "dual carbon" goals, cutting carbon from commercial vehicles has become an industry focus, and some results have already been achieved in electrifying commercial buses; in future, efforts to promote new energy in the freight vehicle segment will be stepped up, and electrification of specialist fields such as municipal sanitation and urban logistics will become a development priority.

　　During the 14th Five-Year Plan, commercial vehicle development will be characterised by lightweighting, digitalisation and intelligence. Autonomous last-mile delivery vehicles will develop rapidly over the next five years; by 2025 China's autonomous last-mile delivery market will reach 60,000 vehicles. (Reporter Zhou Peipei)

# China Association of Automobile Manufacturers: 2021 vehicle sales expected to reach 27 million units

Source: Yangcheng Evening News | 14 July 2021 15:32

Yangcheng Evening News | 14 July 2021 15:32

###### Original headline: 2021 vehicle sales expected to reach 27 million units

Loading

By Yangcheng Evening News reporter Qi Yaoqi

　　A China Association of Automobile Manufacturers information briefing held recently in Beijing showed that from January to June this year the vehicle market was broadly stable, continuing to consolidate the foundations for the industry's development. On market conditions, June vehicle production and sales fell year over year, with commercial vehicles falling more than passenger vehicles, but new energy vehicles and exports remained strong, both setting new sales records.

　　On first-half market conditions, despite adverse factors such as the chip shortage and rising raw material prices, passenger vehicle sales still exceeded 10 million units; cumulative new energy vehicle sales already matched the full-year 2019 level, with battery electric vehicles exceeding 1 million units, and new energy vehicle penetration rose from 5.4% at the start of the year to 9.4% in the first half, with June penetration already above 12%, showing that the new momentum is gradually broadening.

　　In June, vehicle production and sales reached 1.943 million and 2.015 million units respectively, down 4.8% and 5.3% month over month and down 16.5% and 12.4% year over year. Compared with the same period in 2019, output rose 2.4% while sales fell 2.2%; the output growth rate fell 7.9 percentage points from May, and the sales growth rate turned from positive to negative compared with May.

　　From January to June, vehicle production and sales reached 12.569 million and 12.891 million units respectively, up 24.2% and 25.6% year over year, with the growth rates falling a further 12.2 and 11 percentage points from January-May. Compared with the same period in 2019, production and sales grew 3.4% and 4.4% year over year, with the growth rates down 0.2 and 1.4 percentage points from January-May.

　　Xu Haidong, deputy chief engineer of the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers, released CAAM's latest revised forecast for the Chinese vehicle market in 2021.

From January to April 2024, BEVs grew 12.4% year over year to 2.94 million units, with growth continuing to slow, while PHEVs grew 86.5% to 1.115 million units, with growth accelerating. According to CAAM data, China's vehicle exports (excluding used vehicles) grew 57.9% year over year to 4.91 million units in 2023, overtaking Japan (about 4.42 million units) to become the world's largest vehicle exporter. ## Detailed introduction

The research firm EVTank, together with the Ivy Economic Research Institute, recently published the "White Paper on the Development of China's New Energy Vehicle Industry (2023)". The white paper's data shows that global new energy vehicle sales reached 10.824 million units in 2022, up 61.6% year over year. EVTank's analysis notes that global vehicle sales were driven mainly by China. In 2022 China's new energy vehicle sales reached 6.884 million units, raising its global share to 63.6%, against just 53.0% in 2021. EVTank states in the white paper that in 2022 sales growth in the European and US new energy vehicle markets fell short of expectations, at just 16.0% and 52.1% year over year respectively, some distance from the forecasts made at the start of the year. EVTank says that in 2023, as the US IRA takes effect, it will pull US new energy vehicle sales on the demand side and to some extent shape the regional competitive landscape at every stage of the global new energy vehicle supply chain. Looking ahead, EVTank expects global new energy vehicle sales to reach 25.422 million and 52.120 million units in 2025 and 2030 respectively, with new energy vehicle penetration continuing to rise and exceeding 50% by 2030.

## 2023 vehicle production and sales passed 30 million units, with new energy market share at 31.6%

2024-01-12 14:23 Source: China Economic Net Reporter: Jiang Zhiwen

In 2023 China's vehicle production and sales reached 30.161 million and 30.094 million units respectively, up 11.6% and 12% year over year, ranking first worldwide for the 15th consecutive year. Of these, new energy production and sales reached 9.587 million and 9.495 million units respectively, up 35.8% and 37.9% year over year, with a market share of 31.6%.

Chen Shihua said total Chinese vehicle sales are expected to exceed 31 million units in 2024, up more than 3% year over year; of these, passenger vehicle sales of 26.8 million units, up 3% year over year, and commercial vehicle sales of 4.2 million units, up 4% year over year. In addition, new energy vehicle sales of 11.5 million units and vehicle exports of 5.5 million units.

　　"In 2009 China's vehicle production and sales both passed the 10-million mark for the first time, making it the world's largest vehicle producer and seller; in 2013 it passed 20 million; in 2017 production and sales reached a cyclical peak, after which the market declined for three consecutive years and entered a period of transition and adjustment; in 2021 it ended the 'three straight declines' and began to recover, and now it has finally achieved the goal of passing 30 million units," said Chen Shihua, deputy secretary general of CAAM.

Source: China Association of Automobile Manufacturers

　　Yesterday (11 January), data released by the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers (CAAM) showed that in 2023 China's vehicle production and sales reached 30.161 million and 30.094 million units respectively, up 11.6% and 12% year over year, ranking first worldwide for the 15th consecutive year; in December alone, production and sales reached 3.079 million and 3.156 million units respectively, up 29.2% and 23.5% year over year. [...] Source: China Association of Automobile Manufacturers

　　By vehicle type, 2023 passenger vehicle exports were 4.14 million units, up 63.7% year over year; commercial vehicle exports were 770,000 units, up 32.2% year over year. Of these, conventional fuel vehicle exports were 3.707 million units, up 52.4% year over year; new energy vehicle exports were 1.203 million units, up 77.6% year over year.

　　Among the top ten vehicle exporters, by growth rate BYD exported 252,000 units, up 3.3-fold year over year; Chery exported 925,000 units, up 1-fold; Great Wall exported 316,000 units, up 82.5%; SAIC Group exported 1.099 million units, the largest vehicle exporter.

　　"Although next year's (2024) opportunity markets are full of unknowns, with some countries and regions launching anti-subsidy investigations and possibly even raising tariffs, we remain fully confident about vehicle exports," said Xu Haidong. "At present we have core advantages in both combustion and electric vehicle products; as service and systems capability are built up, Chinese vehicle exports can still stay ahead, and exports are expected to reach 5.5 million units in 2024."

"Twin-engine drive": new energy vehicles step up to the 9.5-million level

　　Notably, China's full-year new energy vehicle production and sales entered the 9.5-million range, ranking first worldwide for the ninth consecutive year. In 2023 new energy production and sales reached 9.587 million and 9.495 million units respectively, up 35.8% and 37.9% year over year, with a market share of 31.6%, 5.9 percentage points higher than the same period the previous year. In December 2023 new energy vehicle production and sales reached 1.172 million and 1.191 million units respectively, up 47.5% and 46.4% year over year, with a market share of 37.7%; new energy passenger vehicles reached market shares of 40.9% and 40.4% of production and sales.

Source: China Association of Automobile Manufacturers

　　"Under the twin effects of policy and the market, new energy vehicles continued to grow rapidly in 2023," Chen Shihua said. In 2023 companies launched many models suited to consumer demand, and combined with the continuing improvement of charging and battery-swap infrastructure, new energy vehicles developed considerably. [...] By drivetrain, 2023 battery electric vehicle sales were 6.685 million units, up 24.6% year over year; plug-in hybrid vehicle sales were 2.804 million units, up 84.7% year over year; fuel cell vehicle sales were 6,000 units, up 72% year over year.

　　In 2023 the top ten enterprise groups by new energy vehicle sales sold 8.241 million units in total, up 47.7% year over year, accounting for 86.8% of total new energy vehicle sales. Of these, the top three sold 5.065 million units, a market share of 53.3%.

　　"Compared with new energy vehicles, the top ten key enterprise groups saw declining market concentration in combustion vehicles," Xu Haidong said. EV start-ups may produce only new energy vehicles and can win a certain market share in that field, but their sales cannot yet reach the top ten in combustion vehicles.

　　That said, "some new innovative companies are still entering and competing head to head with existing companies in the new energy market, which also brings consumers better products and choices," Xu Haidong said. Competition also drives the automotive industry to grow stronger and promotes everyone's positive development.

　　On future vehicle development trends, Chen Shihua said total Chinese vehicle sales are expected to exceed 31 million units in 2024, up more than 3% year over year; of these, passenger vehicle sales of 26.8 million units, up 3% year over year, and commercial vehicle sales of 4.2 million units, up 4% year over year. In addition, new energy vehicle sales of 11.5 million units and vehicle exports of 5.5 million units. (China Economic Net reporter Jiang Zhiwen)

According to data released by the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers (hereafter CAAM), in 2024 cumulative vehicle production and sales reached 31.282 million and 31.436 million units respectively, up 3.7% and 4.5% year over year; China's total vehicle production and sales have ranked first worldwide for 16 consecutive years.

　　Xu Haidong, executive deputy secretary general of the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers, said that in 2025 the automotive industry will have five favourable factors: the accelerating release of macro-policy vitality; the continuing effect of the "two new" policies; the extension of the new energy purchase tax exemption; the continuing expansion of overseas market space; and the marked results of supply-side reform.

　　CAAM forecasts total Chinese vehicle sales of 32.9 million units in 2025, up 4.7% year over year. Of these, passenger vehicle sales of 28.9 million units, up 4.9% year over year; commercial vehicle sales of 4 million units, up 3.3% year over year; new energy vehicles at 16 million units, up 24.4% year over year; and export sales of 6.2 million units, up 5.8% year over year.

# CAAM: China's 2022 new energy vehicle sales exceeded 6.8 million units; XPeng responds to Wang Fengying becoming CEO | 36Kr New Energy Daily 0112

Author | Yang Ziyan; Editor | Zhang Lin

36Kr's To B industry team compiles the day's main new energy news for readers. The 12 January new energy industry daily is as follows:

## Policy and market, first thing

### CAAM: China's 2022 new energy vehicle sales exceeded 6.8 million units, up 93.4% year over year

According to China Association of Automobile Manufacturers statistical analysis, China's 2022 vehicle sales were 26.864 million units, up 2.1% year over year, against 3.8% growth in the same period of 2021; new energy vehicles continued their explosive growth, with 2022 sales exceeding 6.8 million units, up 93.4% year over year and market share rising to 25.6%, moving gradually into a phase of full market-driven expansion and a new stage of development and growth. China's December vehicle sales fell 8.4% year over year.

"2022 automotive industry production and sales"

### CAAM's Xu Haidong: new energy vehicle makers reaching sales above 100,000 units may become profitable

The China Association of Automobile Manufacturers held an information briefing on 12 January, at which Xu Haidong, CAAM deputy chief engineer, said that it is a fact that Chinese new energy vehicle manufacturers are generally not yet profitable, but that new energy and intelligent connectivity are the automotive industry's future direction.

"If a company does not transform, it should not be in this industry in future," Xu Haidong noted. As the new energy vehicle market grows rapidly the pie also grows larger, and once the relevant makers can reach sales of 100,000 units or more they may become profitable - Tesla began making a profit after global sales exceeded 400,000 units.

"CAAM's Xu Haidong: new energy vehicle makers reaching sales above 100,000 units may become profitable"

### Interest stays high as subsidies wind down; several separator makers say orders are unaffected

Several separator manufacturers including Yunnan Energy New Material, Cangzhou Mingzhu and Meilian New Materials reportedly say downstream demand for separators remains hot, order books are full and product prices are stable, with no felt impact from the withdrawal of the subsidy policy. One industry figure said separator makers mostly sign long-term contracts with battery plants, so removing subsidies has little effect on them; combined with growing demand in energy storage and overseas markets, separator supply and demand is expected to remain tightly balanced for the whole year. ## New developments in the battery industry

### Pret: subsidiary signs strategic cooperation agreement with HiNa Battery to advance mass production of sodium-ion batteries

According to a Pret announcement, the company's controlled subsidiary Highstar recently signed a "Strategic Cooperation Agreement" with HiNa Battery on "sodium-ion battery product development and market promotion". The two sides will cooperate closely on sodium-ion battery materials, process routes and manufacturing, to advance mass production of sodium-ion battery products as soon as possible, focusing on target markets such as household energy storage, backup power and special-purpose vehicles and jointly bringing in core customer applications.

Highstar also began construction in December 2022 of a 1.3 GWh intelligent automated production line compatible with both sodium-ion and lithium-ion batteries.

"Pret: subsidiary signs strategic cooperation agreement with HiNa Battery to advance mass production of sodium-ion batteries"

### Iteration accelerates as multiple photovoltaic cell technologies meet head-on

On the 11th LONGi Green Energy disclosed that it plans to redirect 4.77 billion yuan of previously raised funds to the Xixian Leye 29 GW-a-year high-efficiency monocrystalline cell project. The project's cell process will adopt the company's in-house developed HPBC high-efficiency cell technology.

Industry figures say that as PERC cells become ubiquitous and approach the theoretical limit of photoelectric conversion efficiency, cell technologies represented by TOPCon, heterojunction (HJT) and HPBC are attracting capital market attention. Photovoltaic cell technology routes iterate quickly, and different routes will meet head-on in 2023 in white-hot competition.

"Iteration accelerates as multiple photovoltaic cell technologies meet head-on"

### Snowway's restructuring plan of more than 6.4 billion yuan passed unanimously at the creditors' meeting

On 11 January the second vote of the ordinary creditors' group at the fifth creditors' meeting in the bankruptcy restructuring case of Yajiang County Snowway Mining Development Co., Ltd was held at the People's Court of the Chengdu High-Tech Industrial Development Zone. It emerged at the meeting that CATL, as the restructuring investor, had put forward a restructuring plan of more than 6.4 billion yuan.

At yesterday's meeting, however, GCL (including GCL Energy Technology and its affiliates), as a creditor, did not vote in favour and objected to the plan. On 12 January the restructuring plan passed unanimously. That also means the ownership of the "sky-high-priced lithium mine" is now very clear, with CATL the eventual winner.

In 2014 annual new energy vehicle sales in mainland China were 74,800 units, 4.2 times the 2013 figure. In 2015, driven by a range of policies, many consumers switched their purchase intentions to new energy, and new energy vehicle sales continued to grow substantially. That year new energy vehicle sales reached 331,100 units, up 340%, making China the world's largest new energy vehicle market. BYD's new energy vehicle sales that year were 61,700 units, overtaking Nissan and Tesla among global new energy vehicle makers to rank first for the first time. In 2014 and 2013 BYD had ranked seventh and fortieth respectively in global new energy sales. In 2016 annual new energy vehicle sales in mainland China were 507,000 units, passing the 500,000 mark for the first time. In 2017 mainland China sold 777,000 new energy vehicles, of which 652,000 were battery electric vehicles.

In 2018 China's annual new energy vehicle sales were 1.256 million units, up 61.7% on 2017, making it the first country in the world whose annual new energy vehicle sales passed the one-million mark. Of these, cumulative new energy passenger vehicle sales were 1.053 million units, with battery electric vehicles accounting for 75%; almost all new energy bus and truck sales were battery electric. In 2019 China's annual new energy vehicle sales reached 1.206 million units, 53% of the global total. Although that global share was down on 2018's 57%, the industry's scale still ranked first in the world. In 2020 China's annual new energy vehicle sales reached 1.367 million units. As of the end of 2020 mainland China's new energy vehicle population reached 4.92 million, 1.75% of all vehicles; of these, the battery electric vehicle population was 4 million, 81.32% of all new energy vehicles.

In 2021 mainland China's annual new energy vehicle sales were 3.521 million units, of which 3.334 million were passenger vehicles and 186,000 commercial vehicles. In 2022 mainland China's annual new energy vehicle sales were 6.887 million units, of which 6.549 million were new energy passenger vehicles and 338,000 new energy commercial vehicles. In 2023 mainland China's annual new energy vehicle sales were 9.495 million units. [...] The main production centres for new energy vehicles in mainland China are Shanghai, Shenzhen and Xi'an, whose combined output accounts for more than 40% of the national total. In 2021 Shanghai's new energy vehicle output was 632,000 units, ranking first; but in 2022 Xi'an's new energy vehicle output reached 1.0152 million units, overtaking Shanghai for the first time; in 2023 Shenzhen's new energy vehicle output reached 1.786 million units, overtaking Xi'an. Besides these, Hefei, Changsha, Guangzhou, Chongqing and Liuzhou are also new energy vehicle industry bases, and the new energy vehicle industries of Zhengzhou, Wuhan, Qingdao, Changchun, Chengdu, Nanjing and Changzhou have also reached a certain scale. Hefei and Liuzhou have gone further, setting a target of more than 3 million units of planned new energy vehicle output by 2025. On output penetration, Xi'an, Changsha and Shenzhen are the top three cities for new energy vehicles' share of local vehicle output.

From 2023 onwards China's new energy vehicle production lines began to expand overseas. GAC, Changan, Neta and Great Wall have successively begun building production bases in Southeast Asia; BYD is also building a production base in Hungary. BYD executives have said a second plant will be established in Europe in 2025. On 26 February 2024 BYD was reported to have approached the Italian government to discuss establishing a second plant in Europe. On 8 July 2024 BYD announced it would build a new plant in Turkey.

### Supporting industries

[edit]

Mainland China is the world's main processing centre for lithium, cobalt and graphite raw materials, which has also created the conditions for a complete new energy vehicle value chain. As of December 2023 mainland China had 1.08 million upstream, midstream and downstream new energy vehicle-related companies, with the Yangtze River Delta, Pearl River Delta, Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei and Chengdu-Chongqing regions being the four city clusters where leading industry cities are most concentrated. Of these, Shanghai and the Yangtze River Delta have 13,000 new energy vehicle-related companies and a complete new energy vehicle component value chain. CATL, founded in 2011, holds numerous battery-related technologies and has led the world in power battery installations since 2017.

## Charging facilities

[edit]

### Charging infrastructure

[edit] [...] The "Medium and Long-Term Development Plan for the Automotive Industry" issued by MIIT in 2017 stated that the automotive industry would transition gradually towards new energy, with a target of 2 million units of annual new energy vehicle output by 2020 and more than 20% of new vehicle output by 2025. In 2018 China's annual new energy vehicle output passed the one-million mark, after which the industry matured and stopped relying excessively on subsidies, government procurement, and tariffs or barriers on foreign-market products. New energy vehicle subsidy levels were tapered appropriately each year and replaced by a "dual-credit" policy for manufacturers. The momentum of new energy vehicle growth also shifted from municipal bus fleet procurement to the private passenger vehicle market. In June that year the "Special Administrative Measures for Foreign Investment Access (Negative List) (2018 edition)", issued by the Ministry of Commerce and the National Development and Reform Commission, stated that foreign-invested enterprises would be allowed to build wholly owned plants producing new energy vehicles. A month after the new policy took effect, Tesla announced it had signed an agreement with the Shanghai Municipal People's Government to build a gigafactory in Shanghai's Lingang New City. As the market has grown and policy has continued to loosen, foreign companies have successively begun cooperating in China's new energy vehicle sector.

### 2021 to the present: a phase of rapid development

[edit]

After 2021, as the country put forward its "dual carbon strategy", mainland China's new energy vehicle population grew substantially, a localised supply chain was essentially established and key technologies were brought in-house. In 2022 domestic Chinese-brand new energy passenger vehicles accounted for 79.9% of total sales, BYD overtook Tesla for the first time to become the world's largest new energy vehicle maker by production and sales, and NIO, Li Auto and XPeng each passed 100,000 deliveries that year, further strengthening brand competitiveness. CAAM publishes full-year 2021 market data: "ending" three consecutive years of decline

On 12 January the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers (hereafter CAAM) formally published sales data for the full year 2021 and for December alone. In this analysis CAAM reviewed several years of cumulative figures across multiple segments, giving a clearer overview of how each sub-segment has developed over the past decade.

Looking at the full-year 2021 figures alone, although the market has been through - and is still going through - adverse factors including chip shortages, rising raw material prices and pandemic fluctuations, China's vehicle market has broadly escaped three consecutive years of decline. CAAM noted: in 2021 China's vehicle production and sales reached 26.082 million and 26.275 million units respectively, up 3.4% and 3.8% year over year, ending the three consecutive years of decline since 2018.

Besides ending three straight years of decline, 2021's more striking feature was the rapid advance of new energy vehicle sales. CAAM data shows that in 2021 new energy vehicle production and sales reached 3.545 million and 3.521 million units respectively, both up 1.6-fold year over year, with market share reaching 13.4%, 8 percentage points higher than the previous year.

New energy vehicle sales passed 200,000 units in March last year, 300,000 in August, 400,000 in November and 530,000 by December, showing sustained growth momentum.

By segment, battery electric vehicles also set a new monthly sales record: in December battery electric vehicle production and sales reached 434,000 and 448,000 units respectively, both up 1.1-fold year over year; plug-in hybrid vehicle production and sales reached 84,000 and 82,000 units, up 1.6-fold and 1.2-fold year over year; fuel cell vehicle production and sales reached 627 and 486 units, up 1.4-fold and 1.1-fold year over year.

Another major highlight was vehicle exports. CAAM data shows that full-year 2021 passenger vehicle exports were 1.614 million units, up 1.1-fold year over year; commercial vehicle exports were 402,000 units, up 70.7% year over year.

CAAM noted in particular: in 2021 vehicle exports were 2.015 million units, up 1-fold year over year, accounting for 7.7% of total vehicle sales, 3.7 percentage points higher than the previous year. [...] In addition, CAAM data shows that in 2021 the top ten companies by vehicle sales sold 22.621 million units in total, 86.1% of total vehicle sales. Among those top ten, compared with the previous year, SAIC, FAW, Dongfeng and BAIC saw sales decline while the others grew, with BYD, Chery, Great Wall and Changan growing faster.

### 03 New energy breaks out, with many players growing the pie

Driven by national policy and market factors, China's new energy vehicles showed an overall "explosion" in 2021.

According to CAAM data, full-year 2021 new energy vehicle sales exceeded 3.5 million units and market share rose to 13.4%. That also owes something to new energy passenger vehicle monthly penetration passing 5% in June 2020 and then climbing steadily for 19 consecutive months.

In 2021 new energy vehicle production and sales reached 3.545 million and 3.521 million units respectively, both up 1.6-fold year over year, the highest growth rate since 2016. In December just passed, new energy passenger vehicles' monthly retail penetration hit a record high of 22.6%.

The top three new energy passenger vehicle makers by full-year sales were BYD, SAIC-GM-Wuling and Tesla, with a wide gap to their followers.

BYD pushed on both the battery electric and plug-in hybrid routes at once, with full-year new energy passenger vehicle sales of 594,000 units, up 231.6% year over year; SAIC-GM-Wuling's MINI EV, aimed at the small low-end market, reached cumulative sales of 550,000 units; Tesla's Shanghai plant reached annual output of 483,000 units, and the brand's deliveries in China were 319,000 units.

Other makers with annual new energy passenger vehicle sales above 100,000 units were Great Wall Motor, GAC Aion and SAIC Group. Among the EV start-ups, XPeng, NIO and Li Auto sold 98,000, 91,000 and 90,000 units respectively, ranking 7th, 9th and 10th.

From the full-year model rankings, of the more than 200 new energy models on the market the top 20 accounted for a combined 65%, showing that best-selling models contribute markedly to the total; the first-placed Wuling Hongguang MINIEV and second-placed Tesla Model Y together accounted for nearly 20% of the new energy market share.

By price band, competition was fiercest among models in the 150,000-200,000 yuan band, while sales in the 200,000-300,000 yuan band lagged behind the below-100,000, 100,000-200,000 and above-300,000 yuan bands overall. [...] In addition, NIO, BYD and others have also taken Chinese electric vehicles to European markets such as Norway.

Among these, vehicle exports performed strongly, with annual exports passing 2 million units for the first time, a breakthrough after hovering around 1 million units for many years; boosted by new energy and favourable export markets, Chinese-brand vehicles' market share has passed 44%, close to its best level ever.

Over the past year the whole industry faced challenges including the global spread of the pandemic, scattered domestic outbreaks and chip shortages, yet still achieved growth:

partly thanks to the low base in the Chinese market over the previous two years; and partly because new energy vehicles, Chinese domestic brands and vehicle exports have become important drivers of the industry's development, with striving Chinese vehicle makers playing an indispensable part.

Reviewing Chinese vehicle makers' 2021 production and sales offers, besides the retrospective, a glimpse of the shifting fortunes among them.

### 01 Southern vehicle makers sweep China's vehicle market

EO Intelligence found that the top three makers by full-year sales - SAIC Group, Changan Automobile and GAC Group - are based in Shanghai, Chongqing and Guangzhou respectively, all southern makers.

On sales, SAIC Group's result was the most striking: with total full-year 2021 sales of 5.464 million units it topped the Chinese vehicle maker sales chart for the 16th time, exceeding the combined total of second-placed Changan Automobile (2.301 million units) and third-placed GAC Group (2.144 million units).

SAIC Group's new energy vehicle sales also reached 733,000 units, topping the new energy sales chart.

In the sales rankings of China's leading listed vehicle makers, northern makers such as Great Wall Motor and FAW Jiefang performed reasonably, but there is no denying that southern makers almost monopolise China's vehicle market.

This is inseparable from the south being China's economic centre of gravity. The cities where the high-selling makers are based are all trillion-yuan GDP cities: Shanghai, Chongqing, Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Wuhan, Hangzhou and others joined the trillion-yuan GDP city club long ago.

Thanks to open and supportive policy, the southern market's uniquely advantageous geography has stimulated economic vitality and driven rapid economic development.

As one of the heavy industries underpinning the national economy, China's automotive industry has gradually migrated to the south, with its developed transport systems and dynamic economy, forming a stable and complete automotive supply chain in the southern market and building high-frequency, mutually trusting cooperation with overseas markets, which has allowed China's automotive industry to flourish in the southern market.

The research firm EVTank, together with the Ivy Economic Research Institute, recently published the "White Paper on the Development of China's New Energy Vehicle Industry (2024)". EVTank's data shows that global new energy vehicle sales reached 14.653 million units in 2023, up 35.4% year over year, of which China's new energy vehicle sales reached 9.495 million units, 64.8% of global sales. Full-year 2023 new energy vehicle sales in the United States and Europe were 2.948 million and 1.468 million units respectively, up 18.3% and 48.0% year over year; EVTank's analysis holds that the European new energy vehicle market's below-expectation growth is substantially related to the tapering of subsidies in Germany and other countries in 2023. Looking ahead, EVTank expects global new energy vehicle sales to reach 18.30 million units in 2024, of which China's new energy vehicle sales will reach 11.80 million units, and global new energy vehicle sales to reach 47.00 million units in 2030.

# CPCA: national new energy passenger vehicle retail sales grew 36.2% year over year in 2023

2024-01-10 17:55:20  Source: Economic Information Daily

On 9 January reporters learned from the China Passenger Car Association (CPCA) that 2023 domestic retail sales of new energy passenger vehicles were 7.736 million units, up 36.2% year over year, with full-year penetration of 35.7%, up 8.1 percentage points. CPCA said China is still a country with low passenger vehicle ownership - just 195 vehicles per thousand people at the end of 2022 - and as the world's car factory it has an enormous pool of potential first-time buyers.

According to CPCA data, China's cumulative passenger vehicle retail sales in 2023 were 21.699 million units, up 5.6% year over year. Cumulative new energy passenger vehicle production in 2023 was 8.920 million units, up 33.7% year over year; cumulative wholesale 8.864 million units, up 36.3%; cumulative retail 7.736 million units, up 36.2%; cumulative exports 1.048 million units, up 72.0%.

From the makers' perspective, the leading makers captured enormous increments. According to CPCA data, the top five companies added 2.29 million units, 97% of the year's 2.35-million increment. BYD, Chery, Geely and Changan all gained both export and domestic new energy increments, while FAW-Volkswagen did well domestically. Other makers had no overall increment, but among joint ventures BMW Brilliance, FAW-Volkswagen and Jiangsu Yueda Kia achieved relatively good year-over-year sales growth, and Volvo Asia Pacific and Chery Jaguar Land Rover also grew.

CPCA said 2023 was a year in which China's automotive industry worked a miracle, with passenger vehicle wholesale and exports at record highs, making people newly aware of the potential of China's automotive industry and its room for market development. With continued contributions from the electrification transition and export growth, China's vehicle production and sales could exceed 40 million units in future.

Notably, China's vehicle exports grew strongly in 2023. [...] Notably, China's vehicle exports grew strongly in 2023.

According to customs data compiled by CPCA, China's vehicle exports ranked first in the world by both volume and value. CPCA's analysis says there is international market demand for more than 60 million vehicles globally, and that improving quality and leading intelligence in Chinese domestic-brand combustion vehicles, together with a new blue ocean of overseas markets created by leading the international electric vehicle trend, have driven China's export growth. At the same time, because export unit prices are high and margins good, domestic brands have earned substantial profits from exports and shared the cost pressure of domestic sales, so export volumes have climbed.

"With China's new energy scale advantages and market expansion needs, more and more Chinese-made new energy product brands are going abroad, their recognition overseas keeps rising, and with service networks continuing to improve, the new energy export market remains favourable with promising prospects," CPCA noted.

On the passenger vehicle market in January 2024, CPCA believes December 2023 saw particularly heavy promotional activity, which brought some purchase demand forward, so January should be a phase of gradually withdrawing promotions and achieving steady sales. But given the low base caused by last year's early Spring Festival and the post-policy-withdrawal adjustment period, January retail sales this year could still grow substantially.

# New energy vehicle sales hit a record in 2021: can 5 million be achieved this year?

Filed: 2022-01-05 09:16:00   Source: Guangzhou Daily    China Youth Net

With China's new energy vehicle market booming, the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, the Ministry of Science and Technology and the National Development and Reform Commission (hereafter the four ministries) recently jointly issued the "Notice of the Ministry of Finance, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, the Ministry of Science and Technology and the National Development and Reform Commission on the 2022 Fiscal Subsidy Policy for the Promotion and Application of New Energy Vehicles" (hereafter the "Notice"). The Notice requires that in 2022 subsidy levels for non-public-sector new energy vehicles taper by 30% from the 2021 basis and public-sector vehicle subsidies taper by 20%, with subsidies removed entirely by 2023.

　　Text, images and tables / Guangzhou Daily all-media reporter Xu Xiaofang

Domestic "EV start-ups" performed strongly in 2021

　　China Association of Automobile Manufacturers data shows that from January to November 2021 new energy vehicle production and sales reached 3.023 million and 2.99 million units respectively, both up 1.7-fold year over year. On 3 January Cui Dongshu, secretary general of CPCA, wrote that from January to November 2021 China's new energy passenger vehicle sales accounted for 52% of the world total, and in November reached 60% - six tenths of global new energy vehicles.

　　Over the past year China's new energy vehicle "EV start-ups" have developed rapidly in sales terms. CAAM statistics show that in the first 11 months of 2021 the main start-ups' sales reached 81.1%, up 226.3% year over year; concentration reached 3.5%, up 2.3% year over year. [...] Of these, XPeng's December 2021 sales set another record, with 16,000 deliveries in the month, up 181% year over year; XPeng's total 2021 deliveries reached 98,155 units, 3.6 times 2020's 27,041. Li Auto delivered 14,087 units in December 2021, up 130% year over year; for the whole of 2021 Li Auto delivered 90,491 units, up 177.4% year over year. As for NIO, it delivered 10,489 new vehicles in December 2021 and 91,429 for the year, up 109.1% year over year.

　　As for BYD, the domestic makers' sales "number one", its December 2021 new energy passenger vehicle sales were 92,823 units, up 236.4% year over year. For the whole of 2021 BYD's cumulative new energy passenger vehicle sales were close to 600,000 units.

　　But against Tesla, the new energy "leader", domestic new energy brands still lag somewhat on sales. In the fourth quarter of 2021 Tesla produced 305,840 new energy vehicles worldwide and delivered 308,600; for the whole of 2021 Tesla produced 930,422 new energy vehicles and delivered 936,172.

　　And with internet giants such as Baidu, Xiaomi, Midea and 360 joining the "car-making race", industry figures note that competition in China's domestic new energy vehicle market will become ever fiercer. CAAM forecasts total Chinese vehicle sales of 27.5 million units in 2022, up 5.4% year over year; of these, passenger vehicle sales of 23 million units, up 8% year over year; commercial vehicle sales of 4.5 million units, down 6% year over year; and new energy vehicle sales of 5 million units, up 47% year over year.

With subsidies cut, makers respond one after another

　　What effect will the Notice's publication have on China's new energy vehicle sales? On this, industry figures say that under the newly published policy the existing purchase subsidy technical indicator framework and threshold requirements remain unchanged for 2022, while the subsidy scale is freed from the previously expected 2-million-unit cap, delivering subsidies throughout the year. The end of 2022 will therefore see a strong increment, boosting total 2022 new energy vehicle sales. [...] Under the 2022 subsidy scheme, in 2021 a battery electric vehicle with a range of 300-400 km could receive a 13,000 yuan subsidy, which falls by 3,900 yuan in 2022; in 2021 a battery electric vehicle with a range above 400 km priced below 300,000 yuan could receive an 18,000 yuan subsidy, which falls by 5,400 yuan in 2022.

　　The major makers have also responded to the new policy one after another. On 31 December 2021 Tesla announced that the rear-wheel-drive versions of the Model 3 and Model Y would rise in price by 10,000 and 21,000 yuan respectively, and because the entire Model Y range is priced above 300,000 yuan after the increase it will not qualify for the national subsidy. As noted on the order page of Tesla's official website, product prices are all post-subsidy starting prices, derived by deducting the estimated 2022 new energy vehicle subsidy from the pre-subsidy starting price. If the price of a configured vehicle exceeds 300,000 yuan the above new energy vehicle subsidy does not apply, and the final subsidy amount is subject to the policy in force at the time of delivery.

　　Besides raising prices, some makers have chosen to introduce price-protection policies. NIO's 2022 purchase subsidy scheme states that users who paid a deposit for an ES8, ES6 or EC6 on or before 31 December 2021 and successfully take delivery before 31 March 2022 can still receive the subsidy at the 2021 national standard, while users after that cannot. XPeng said users paying a deposit between 1 and 10 January 2022 can enjoy the same subsidy policy as in 2021, with XPeng bearing the subsidy difference.

　　A Shengang Securities research note said the pace of subsidy tapering is in line with expectations, that 2022 is the last year of a steady subsidy exit, and that non-subsidy policies such as the dual-credit scheme will take the baton in driving new energy vehicle penetration higher.

　　It is worth noting that regions are currently actively introducing policies to promote new energy vehicle development. On 30 December 2021 the Guangzhou Municipal Development and Reform Commission issued Guangzhou's 14th Five-Year Plan for the innovative development of intelligent and new energy vehicles, proposing to issue comprehensive subsidies for individual consumers buying new energy vehicles at an appropriate time, and to study incentive policies for after subsidies end, so as to promote orderly development of new energy vehicle use in the private sector.

# JD Power study: new energy "new" models underperform carryover models on quality; makers accelerating launches still need to watch quality

The Leapmotor T03, Neta U, XPeng P5, Volkswagen ID.4 X, NIO ES6 and AITO M5 each took first place in their segments

2023 China NEV-IQS CN

1 June 2023, Shanghai - JD Power, the world's leading consumer insights and market research organisation, today formally released the 2023 China New Energy Vehicle Initial Quality StudySM (NEV-IQS). The study shows that in 2023 the new energy vehicle industry's overall quality problem count was 173 PP100, an increase of 21 PP100 on 2022. Within that, the proportions of design-defect problems and problems specific to new energy vehicles both increased, reflecting that while new energy vehicles are developing rapidly, quality stability still needs improving.

The JD Power China New Energy Vehicle Initial Quality Study (NEV-IQS) began in 2019, based on JD Power's industry-standard IQS new vehicle quality study framework and supplemented for problems specific to new energy vehicles; it counts and measures the quality problems new energy vehicle owners encounter during 2 to 6 months of ownership. Initial quality is expressed as problems per 100 vehicles (PP100); the lower the count, the better the quality.

The study shows that in 2023 the new energy vehicle industry's overall quality level was worse than last year. Within that, new models' quality problems were more pronounced, 15 PP100 higher than carryover models at 184 PP100, with new models lagging carryover models on quality in almost every problem category, and especially on driving experience, where they lagged by 3.6 PP100. In fact, carryover models' quality problem count (169 PP100) also rose on last year: as the new energy vehicle market's scale expands rapidly, the composition of buyers is shifting, which also brings changes in perceived quality levels. [...] Yang Tao, general manager of JD Power's automotive product division for China, said: "Competition in the new energy vehicle market is escalating, with makers continually launching new models and completing their product matrices to capture market share. In this year's study we noted that new models' quality performance is still less stable than carryover models', and the factors behind that are multiple: the pressure of compressed new vehicle development cycles, and also the quality-control and integration problems brought by increasingly complex technology features. New energy vehicles have completed the transformation from zero to one, and the key to winning future competition will return to product quality; while makers accelerate launches, they still need to attend to user experience and quality management."

Other findings of the study:

 Interior odour and tyre noise have been top quality problems for five consecutive years: unpleasant smells inside the vehicle topped the complaints at 9.3 PP100, with excessive tyre noise second at 7.5 PP100; these two problems have topped the chart for five consecutive years. They were also top quality complaints in the 2022 China Initial Quality Study (IQS), reflecting that Chinese vehicle consumers are consistent in their basic quality requirements, whether for new energy or combustion vehicles.

 The mid-size SUV segment has become the fiercest battleground between battery electric and plug-in hybrid: mid-size SUVs are currently the segment with the largest sales share for both battery electric and plug-in hybrid, and the segment with the densest stream of launches for both. Mid-size SUVs' share of sales rose markedly on the previous year (+8.7%), and especially mid-size plug-in hybrid SUVs, whose sales share rose 7.3 percentage points. On quality, mid-size plug-in hybrid SUVs performed better on basic problems (such as driving experience, HVAC and seats), while mid-size battery electric SUVs had better powertrain quality.\

 Replacement buyers are the fastest-growing share and have the highest transaction price: in 2023 replacement buyers were the fastest-growing share of the new energy vehicle market, and their average transaction price was higher than that of first-time and additional buyers, making them a group the new energy vehicle market needs to watch closely. At present, however, replacement buyers' overall satisfaction with new energy vehicle quality is lower (180 PP100), with quality complaints 6 and 15 PP100 higher than first-time and additional buyers respectively. In the mainstream battery electric and mainstream plug-in hybrid segments, replacement buyers' quality complaints were above the segment average; only in the luxury segment were replacement buyers' quality complaints lower.

# Ending three straight declines! China's 2021 vehicle sales grew 3.8% and new energy vehicle sales passed 3.5 million units

21 Auto, Zuo Maoxuan 2022-01-12 15:18

Ending three straight declines! China's 2021 vehicle sales grew 3.8%, with three highlights pushing China towards becoming an "automotive power"

21st Century Business Herald reporter Zuo Maoxuan, Beijing - After three consecutive years of decline, China's vehicle market finally returned to growth in 2021.

On 12 January, data published by MIIT at a press conference on the automotive industry's development in 2021 showed that in 2021 China's vehicle production and sales reached 26.082 million and 26.275 million units respectively, up 3.4% and 3.8% year over year.

China's vehicle market began declining in July 2018, with vehicle sales falling 2.8%, 8.2% and 1.9% in 2018, 2019 and 2020 respectively.

In 2021 China's automotive industry also faced challenges including the continued global spread of the pandemic, scattered domestic outbreaks, and supply shortfalls caused by the chip shortage; but because of the low base of the previous two years it achieved slight recovery growth to some extent.

It should be noted that, looking at the industry's month-by-month performance through the year, only January-April sales were higher than the same period last year, while production and sales in the following eight months all fell year over year. However, as pressure on automotive chip supply gradually eased, the pace of recovery in the fourth quarter was better than expected.

"China's total vehicle production and sales have ranked first worldwide for 13 consecutive years, and we have made enormous progress on 'electrification, connectivity and intelligence'. China's position as a major automotive country has been further consolidated and it is moving towards becoming an automotive power," said Fu Bingfeng, executive vice chairman and secretary general of the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers.

New energy vehicles, Chinese brands and vehicle exports were the highlights of China's automotive industry development in 2021.

Full-year new energy vehicle sales exceeded 3.5 million units and market share rose to 13.4%, further demonstrating that the new energy vehicle market has shifted from policy-driven to market-pulled. [...] In 2021 Chinese-brand passenger vehicles sold 9.543 million units in total, up 23.1% year over year, 44.4% of total passenger vehicle sales, with share up 6.0 percentage points on the same period the previous year. Among the major foreign brands, compared with the previous year French passenger vehicle sales growth was the most marked and American brands also grew at a relatively fast double-digit rate, while German, Japanese and Korean brands all declined - Korean brands falling most, with German and Japanese brands mainly affected by supply shortfalls caused by the chip shortage.

Within that, Chinese brands' market shares of sedans, SUVs and MPVs were 31.7%, 52.3% and 68.3% respectively; compared with the previous year Chinese brands' sedan and SUV market shares both grew while their MPV share fell.

As household incomes gradually rise, China's vehicle market shows a clear consumption-upgrading trend. In 2021 premium-brand passenger vehicles sold 3.472 million units, up 20.7% year over year, 14.2 percentage points above the passenger vehicle growth rate, and 16.2% of total passenger vehicle sales, 1.9 percentage points higher than the previous year.

#### New energy vehicle production and sales both passed 3.5 million units for the first time

New energy vehicles became the automotive industry's biggest bright spot, with their market development moving from a policy-driven to a market-pulled new stage of development and showing a healthy pattern of improvement in both market scale and quality of development.

In 2021 new energy vehicle production and sales reached 3.545 million and 3.521 million units respectively, both up 1.6-fold year over year, with market share reaching 13.4%, 8 percentage points higher than the previous year. The 2021 new energy vehicle market growth rate was the highest since 2016.

Looking at the new energy vehicle trend, it maintained strong production and sales throughout the year: monthly sales passed 200,000 units from March, 300,000 in August, 400,000 in November and 530,000 in December, showing sustained growth momentum.

Among the main new energy vehicle categories, compared with the same period a year earlier, both battery electric and plug-in hybrid vehicle production and sales showed rapid growth momentum.

In addition, new energy vehicles are being accepted and recognised by more and more consumers and are entering the private consumption market faster, driving further growth in production and sales. [...] Full-year new energy vehicle sales exceeded 3.5 million units and market share rose to 13.4%, further demonstrating that the new energy vehicle market has shifted from policy-driven to market-pulled.

Driven by factors such as the recovery of international markets and improving competitiveness of Chinese brands, China's vehicle exports performed strongly, repeatedly setting new records from April onwards, with annual exports exceeding 2 million units for the first time - a breakthrough after hovering around 1 million units for many years. Within that, new energy vehicle exports performed strongly: in 2021 new energy vehicle exports were 310,000 units, up 3-fold year over year.

In addition, boosted by new energy and favourable export markets, Chinese-brand vehicles' market share has passed 44%, close to its best level ever.

"In 2022 China will continue to do solid work on the 'six stabilities' and 'six guarantees', keep improving people's livelihoods, work to stabilise the macroeconomy and keep economic performance within a reasonable range. Against that backdrop, vehicle market demand will remain stable; and as supply-side problems such as the chip shortage and high raw material prices gradually improve in the new year, the vehicle market is expected to continue a steady, improving trend in 2022, with full-year production and sales performing better than in 2021," CAAM said.

Last December CAAM made a forecast for the 2022 vehicle market. CAAM forecast total Chinese vehicle sales of 27.5 million units in 2022, up 5.4% year over year; of these, passenger vehicle sales of 23 million units, up 8% year over year; commercial vehicle sales of 4.5 million units, down 6% year over year; and new energy vehicle sales of 5 million units, up 47% year over year.

#### Chinese-brand passenger vehicles reach a 44.4% market share

In 2021 passenger vehicle production and sales reached 21.408 million and 21.482 million units respectively, up 7.1% and 6.5% year over year, 3.7 and 2.7 percentage points above the industry rates. Boosted by a strong domestic consumer market, China's passenger vehicle market has exceeded 20 million units for seven consecutive years.

Looking at how passenger vehicle sales changed through the year, the low base early in the year meant the passenger vehicle market showed substantial growth, but as the chip supply shortfall gradually emerged, compounded by the rapid rise in the comparison base, the passenger vehicle market began to decline and the fall widened. Entering the fourth quarter, as the chip problem gradually eased, the passenger vehicle market stabilised and the decline gradually narrowed.

BYD becoming the year's new energy sales champion is not the least bit surprising. In April 2022 BYD announced it would stop selling combustion vehicles, becoming the world's first vehicle brand to do so. The data shows BYD's full-year 2022 vehicle sales were 1.7999 million units, up 208.2% year over year.

In 2022 BYD ended nearly 40 years of joint-venture brands topping China's vehicle sales chart, and with a huge margin of more than 500,000 units took back from Tesla the crown of the world's largest new energy vehicle seller. It was recently reported that BYD chairman Wang Chuanfu had set the company's 2023 sales target at 4 million units. BYD responded that, given the pandemic's impact, there is much uncertainty in the market, consumer demand and the supply chain system, so the company's 2023 sales target is hard to judge. [...] Besides BYD, GAC Aion's strong rise was also a major highlight of the 2022 new energy vehicle market. In March 2022, at a GAC Group results briefing, general manager Feng Xingya said GAC Aion aimed to become the leading new energy vehicle brand and to turn today's "NIO-XPeng-Li" into "Aion-XPeng-NIO". The data shows that in 2022 GAC Aion sold a cumulative 273,800 units, up 115.6% year over year, exceeding its 2022 sales target of "secure 200,000, challenge 250,000", with sales far above the "NIO-XPeng-Li" trio.

Great Wall Motor was the only maker on the chart to decline, with full-year 2022 sales down 7.5% year over year to 123,900 units. As is well known, Great Wall Motor has four passenger vehicle brands - Haval, ORA, WEY and Tank - of which ORA is the only one selling new energy vehicles, with three models on sale: the ORA Good Cat, ORA Ballet Cat and ORA Lightning Cat, while Haval and WEY also have plug-in hybrid models. The data shows 2022 ORA Good Cat sales were 61,094 units, nearly half of Great Wall's new energy vehicle sales. As for the much-watched WEY brand, its sales were dire: the Latte DHT-PHEV sold 9,654 units for the year and the Mocha DHT-PHEV 5,756 units.

On 8 December Great Wall Motor announced adjustments to its brands' organisational structure. It explained that WEY and Tank, and ORA and SALOON, would adopt a dual-brand operating model, fully integrated in organisational management. After integration, Tank brand CEO Liu Yanzhao would also serve as WEY CEO, pushing into premium new energy and global markets; ORA and SALOON would focus on battery electric, with SALOON brand CEO Wen Fei serving as CEO of both SALOON and ORA. Great Wall Motor said this brand marketing organisation adjustment is not simply merger logic but a systematic adjustment spanning brand management, channel operations, sales management and aftersales service. Whether the brand organisation adjustment can have a positive effect on Great Wall Motor's sales remains to be verified by the market.

In 2022 Li Auto's deliveries ranked first among the "NIO-XPeng-Li" trio, delivering 133,200 units for the year, up 47.2% year over year. Of these, Li Auto delivered 21,233 units in December, a record monthly delivery high and the first start-up brand to deliver more than 20,000 in a month. [...] The biggest personnel change at Li Auto that year was the departure of "number two" Shen Yanan. As a Li Auto co-founder, Shen Yanan had been president since 2015 and handled almost all of Li Auto's other businesses, second in authority only to Li Xiang. On 9 December Li Auto announced that co-founder, executive director and president Shen Yanan would cease to hold those positions from 2023 and would leave Li Auto at the end of June 2023.

For XPeng, 2022 could be described as a triumphant first half and a disappointing second. In the first half of 2022 XPeng delivered a cumulative 69,000 new vehicles, up 124% year over year, the highest-selling start-up brand. From the second half, however, XPeng began to show weakness. In September 2022 the XPeng G9 launched, seen as an "important move" in XPeng's push into the mid-to-high-end market; yet it was criticised straight after launch for having numerous and jumbled configurations, fuzzy positioning and a price far above expectations with almost no pleasant surprises, with some owners even cancelling orders.

The G9's failure was the trigger: in October XPeng went through its largest-ever organisational restructuring, with co-founder and president Xia Heng resigning from the board while remaining president focused on product; He Xiaopeng would sharply reduce his direct involvement in ecosystem companies such as XPeng AeroHT and strengthen his management of XPeng's strategy, product planning and R&D.

Finally, on the joint-venture brands, both FAW-Volkswagen and SAIC Volkswagen made the chart, the former up 41.7% year over year and the latter up 50.3%. At present Volkswagen's performance in the electric vehicle market is clearly better than other German and Japanese brands', having launched five new energy models - the ID.4, ID.6X and ID.3 - in 2021, a clear advantage over other brands' electric products converted from combustion platforms. Between FAW-Volkswagen and SAIC Volkswagen, the former performed clearly better than the latter, though affected by the pandemic and component supply.

# First in the world in production and sales for eight consecutive years, China's new energy vehicles keep growing rapidly

2023-01-13 15:30:14  Source: Xinhuanet

Xinhua, Beijing, 13 January - Headline: First in the world in production and sales for eight consecutive years, China's new energy vehicles keep growing rapidly

　　Xinhua reporter Zhang Xinxin

　　Data released recently by the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers shows that China's new energy vehicle production and sales have ranked first in the world for eight consecutive years, maintaining a "fast lane" development posture.

　　Chen Shihua, deputy secretary general of the China Association of Automobile Manufacturers, said China's new energy vehicles are gradually entering a phase of full market-driven expansion. In 2023, problems such as the chip supply shortage are expected to ease considerably; as existing and incremental policies work together and support facilities improve faster, the domestic vehicle market will show a steady, improving trend and new energy vehicles will continue to grow rapidly.

　　On 12 January train X8186, carrying 50 domestically produced new energy vehicles, departed Guangzhou International Port station for Europe. This was the first China-Europe freight train of domestically produced new energy vehicles to leave Guangdong, marking wider channels for new energy vehicle exports.

　　Over the past year, meeting multiple challenges, the new energy vehicle industry maintained rapid development and became an important force in stabilising industry and the economy. The data shows that in 2022 China's new energy vehicle production and sales reached 7.058 million and 6.887 million units respectively, up 96.9% and 93.4% year over year, with a market share of 25.6%. In December 2022 alone, new energy vehicle production and sales reached 795,000 and 814,000 units.

　　The industry's rapid development owes much to the twin effects of policy and the market. Over the year, from establishing "red light" early-warning for vehicle companies' component inventories and a "red-yellow-blue" early-warning coordination mechanism for bulk raw material supply, to strengthening the value chain's digitalisation, policies supporting industry development came in succession and helped companies overcome the pandemic's effects. Extending the new energy vehicle purchase tax exemption and similar measures effectively stimulated market enthusiasm. [...] China's new energy vehicle industry has now entered a new phase of large-scale rapid development, and must maintain its advantages and press ahead. But it should also be recognised that although new energy vehicle production momentum is steady, domestic market growth momentum still needs raising further, and industry development needs stronger guidance at the macro level.

　　Industry figures note that in market terms new energy vehicle development faces competition from traditional combustion vehicles and international brands' new energy vehicles; as some makers announce price cuts, the market landscape may adjust and competition will intensify further. The immediate priority is to strengthen the profitability, in-house innovation capability and overall competitiveness of the domestic new energy vehicle value chain. At the same time it is important to guard against the risk of structural overcapacity in whole vehicles and power batteries, avoid signs of blind expansion and overheated investment in the new energy vehicle industry, further pursue appropriately paced development of domestic lithium resources, and promote power battery recycling to resolve the raw material supply-demand "contradiction". Technological innovation in power batteries and key components should be strengthened, the value chain's competitiveness raised, frontier technologies positioned and product quality improved.

　　Reporters learned from MIIT that in 2023 it will work to strengthen the new energy vehicle industry, use market-based methods to support strong companies growing bigger and stronger and supporting industries developing, work to stabilise big-ticket consumption such as vehicles, implement a new energy vehicle leading-and-strengthening-foundations programme, and carry out intelligent connected vehicle access pilots. It will also step up efforts to optimise the value chain layout, improve the standards system and promote steady industry development.
