Differentiated price bands and competitive new energy models won BYD consumers' votes in hard cash. In addition, BYD has actively expanded into developed European markets such as Norway, riding the decarbonisation wave to take Chinese electric vehicles overseas.

### 03 New energy breaks out, with many players growing the pie

Driven by national policy and market factors, China's new energy vehicles showed an overall "explosion" in 2021.

According to CAAM data, full-year 2021 new energy vehicle sales exceeded 3.5 million units and market share rose to 13.4%. That also owes something to new energy passenger vehicle monthly penetration passing 5% in June 2020 and then climbing steadily for 19 consecutive months.

In 2021 new energy vehicle production and sales reached 3.545 million and 3.521 million units respectively, both up 1.6-fold year over year, the highest growth rate since 2016. In December just passed, new energy passenger vehicles' monthly retail penetration hit a record high of 22.6%.

The top three new energy passenger vehicle makers by full-year sales were BYD, SAIC-GM-Wuling and Tesla, with a wide gap to their followers.

BYD pushed on both the battery electric and plug-in hybrid routes at once, with full-year new energy passenger vehicle sales of 594,000 units, up 231.6% year over year; SAIC-GM-Wuling's MINI EV, aimed at the small low-end market, reached cumulative sales of 550,000 units; Tesla's Shanghai plant reached annual output of 483,000 units, and the brand's deliveries in China were 319,000 units.

Other makers with annual new energy passenger vehicle sales above 100,000 units were Great Wall Motor, GAC Aion and SAIC Group. Among the EV start-ups, XPeng, NIO and Li Auto sold 98,000, 91,000 and 90,000 units respectively, ranking 7th, 9th and 10th.

From the full-year model rankings, of the more than 200 new energy models on the market the top 20 accounted for a combined 65%, showing that best-selling models contribute markedly to the total; the first-placed Wuling Hongguang MINIEV and second-placed Tesla Model Y together accounted for nearly 20% of the new energy market share.

By price band, competition was fiercest among models in the 150,000-200,000 yuan band, while sales in the 200,000-300,000 yuan band lagged behind the below-100,000, 100,000-200,000 and above-300,000 yuan bands overall. [...] In addition, NIO, BYD and others have also taken Chinese electric vehicles to European markets such as Norway.

SAIC is also pushing hard in intelligent electric vehicles: its premium intelligent electric brand IM Motors has completed volume line-off of its first model, the IM L7; its Rising Auto has also been formally established, positioned in the mid-to-high-end intelligent electric vehicle market; and SAIC is actively investing in L4 Robotaxis and L4 intelligent heavy trucks for Yangshan Port, steadily increasing its investment in innovation.

There were weaknesses too - the joint-venture brands SAIC Volkswagen and SAIC-GM sold 1.24 million and 1.33 million units for the year, down 17.5% and 9.3% year over year respectively -

but for the group as a whole to recover quickly after disruptions such as the chip shortage and rising raw material prices was no small feat, and the past year's "steady performance" also owes much to long-accumulated technology and industrial depth.

By comparison, BYD showed fierce catch-up momentum in 2021, becoming the fastest-growing and fastest-improving vehicle maker with a high sales growth rate of 73.3% - more like a dark horse that had built up strength over time, outperforming expectations in both the vehicle sales market and the capital market.

Over the past year BYD's total annual vehicle sales reached 740,000 units, of which new energy vehicles alone accounted for 604,000, 81.6% of all sales, with new energy sales up 218.3% year over year. BYD's new energy vehicle sales growth drove growth in the overall business and at one point pushed its market capitalisation past the 900-billion mark, reaching 929.9 billion yuan.

Focusing on new energy passenger vehicles, BYD, SAIC-GM-Wuling and Tesla China were the top three by full-year new energy sales, with BYD's 594,000 units securing the top spot in Chinese new energy. SAIC-GM-Wuling and Tesla took second and third with 431,000 and 321,000 units respectively.

BYD, which started out making vehicle batteries and has been grinding away at new energy vehicles since 2008, is finally laughing.

After all, not everyone who caught the same tailwind of the "dual carbon" goals and energy saving and emissions reduction has been able to reach scale sales quickly and win market recognition.

That gap is even more marked among Chinese domestic brands. Although BYD, Geely Automobile and Great Wall Motor were evenly matched on sales at the start of 2021, when BYD's monthly sales later passed 90,000 units the other two were selling fewer than 20,000 a month. [...] Among the six EV start-ups, as XPeng's and Li Auto's mainstay models began ramping up, their monthly sales are gradually opening a gap over the other four.

Taking 10,000 units a month as the dividing line, the six EV start-ups clearly fall into two camps: XPeng, Li Auto, NIO and Hozon all passed 10,000 a month, while Leapmotor's and WM Motor's monthly sales were in the 5,000-7,000 range.

Apart from NIO, whose monthly sales fluctuate considerably and are therefore unstable, the start-ups' first tier is relatively stable.

The six state-owned vehicle groups' December new energy sales failed to pass 60,000 units, a wide gap against BYD's 90,000 on its own. Among them GAC Group's new energy brand GAC Aion performed best, with the best-selling AION S reaching monthly retail sales of 7,800 units and the AION Y 6,700 units. Changan Automobile passed 10,000 a month on the strength of a single model, the Benben E-Star, but lacked follow-on new energy models.

FAW Group's Bestune NAT was December's biggest dark horse, rising from sales in the hundreds in November to more than 5,800 in December, which also helped FAW overtake SAIC and BAIC on December new energy sales.

However, as the new energy subsidy policy begins the "countdown" to full withdrawal, new energy vehicles' price advantage may weaken somewhat.

On the one hand, although subsidies are being reduced, the state is still actively promoting new energy vehicle adoption through measures such as advancing charging infrastructure construction and setting up carbon quota management; on the other, makers are preparing their expectations and responses to the subsidy taper.

In future new energy vehicles will shift gradually from policy promotion to market drive, forcing faster technology iteration in China's new energy vehicle industry and forcing makers to offer better mass-production products and raise their competitiveness at the point of sale.

In fact, besides electrification, intelligence has also become a mainstream direction for makers' development - after all, every car-making company harbours an "Apple dream".

### 04 Conclusion

Under the influence of the pandemic, carbon neutrality, chip shortages and many other factors, 2021 thus exited anything but "calmly".

Exports and new energy drove China's vehicle market in 2021, but in the 2022 that follows, Chinese vehicle makers are about to face more complex challenges and uncertainties.

The entry of all sorts of new players has broken the existing pattern of the vehicle and mobility market, and also signals that the core competitive battleground of the future will inevitably revolve around intelligent automotive business models.
